holidays.name: National Pigs in a Blanket Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the glorious union of little sausages wrapped in cozy pastry blankets. Party platters everywhere rejoice, and cocktail weenies get their moment in the spotlight.
holidays.origin: Like many American food holidays, it emerged from food-lover and social media circles rather than any official proclamation, honoring a party snack that has been popular in the United States for decades.
holidays.funFact: In the United Kingdom, 'pigs in blankets' means sausages wrapped in bacon and served at Christmas dinner, while the American version uses dough or crescent rolls.

holidays.name: National Pet Parents Day
holidays.description: A day for people to celebrate being the devoted servants of their furry, scaly, or feathered overlords. Expect extra treats, belly rubs, and an unreasonable number of photos of your pet.
holidays.origin: Created by pet-industry and animal lovers as an unofficial observance, held on the last Sunday of April in some years and widely shared on April 24 on social media.
holidays.funFact: Surveys regularly find that a majority of pet owners consider their pets to be members of the family, and many include them in holiday cards.

holidays.name: World Day for Laboratory Animals
holidays.description: An international awareness day highlighting the animals used in scientific research and calling for better welfare, reduced use, and alternatives to animal testing.
holidays.origin: Started in 1979 by the National Anti-Vivisection Society in the UK, and observed on April 24 to coincide with the birthday of founder Lord Hugh Dowding, who was a prominent anti-vivisection advocate.
holidays.funFact: Lord Dowding was the Royal Air Force commander who led Fighter Command in the Battle of Britain, yet he became a passionate animal welfare campaigner after the war.

holidays.name: Arbor Day Adjacent: Teddy Bear Picnic Day Vibes (Hug a Teddy Day Celebrations)
holidays.description: A cuddly unofficial observance where grown adults are encouraged to dig out their old stuffed animals and have a picnic with them. Sandwiches optional, honey strongly encouraged.
holidays.origin: Teddy bear celebrations trace back to 1902, when President Theodore Roosevelt refused to shoot a captive bear on a hunting trip, inspiring the toy that bears his nickname.
holidays.funFact: The 1907 song 'The Teddy Bears' Picnic' was originally an instrumental tune, and lyrics were added in 1932.

holidays.name: Union Soldiers Day Alternative: Dance Day Debate (National Skipping Day Energy)
holidays.description: A playful unofficial occasion for skipping, twirling, and doing the 'Carlton' dance in public places without shame. Co-workers may be alarmed, but joy is the goal.
holidays.origin: Born from internet-era fun-day calendars that encourage spontaneous silliness and movement on random spring dates.
holidays.funFact: Skipping is one of the first complex gaits that children master, typically around age four or five, and many adults forget how to do it.
